doc.title: Ralph Humphrey interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 11, 2003

title: Growing up near Berkeley, his pianist mother and clarinet first
summary: Born in a Berkeley hospital but raised in Richmond; his mother was a pianist who accompanied his clarinet playing, and he urges students to learn a melodic instrument.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Okay. How did that work. You said you were born in Berkeley but you didn’t live there?
It was just the hospital was in Berkeley. I lived nearby in a place called Richmond, so the Bay Area, I grew up in the Bay Area of California.

She was a pianist. She could have had perhaps a professional career when she was younger but circumstances didn’t allow it. But she carried on as a pianist and played the classics and then ended up accompanying me when I was playing clarinet, doing the festivals and things like that.
Oh so you are a clarinet player?
I was a clarinet player first, yeah. Learned my music on the clarinet. Notes and melodies are really important.
Yes. That helps shape the way you hear music.
I think it has a lot to do with it, I really do. I encourage all my students to take some melodic instrument. I think the ideal instrument is the piano, for just about anybody.
